extracted.intended_audience: inventors and patent applicants; patent office officials and practitioners (historical U.S. patent law audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of statutory requirements, procedural rules, and formalities for obtaining, issuing, recording, and enforcing patents under early U.S. patent statutes (establishing the Patent Office, application/examination rules, fees, models, caveats, assignments, and remedies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements (novelty/usefulness/prior public use/publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person having discovered or invented any new and useful art, machine, manufacture, or composition of matter, or any new and useful improvement ... not known or used by others before his discovery or invention thereof, and not, at the time of his application for a patent, in public use or on sale, with his consent or allowance, may make application ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner shall make an examination and shall not issue a patent if the invention had been invented or discovered by any other person prior to applicant, or had been patented or described in any printed publication in this or any foreign country, or had been in public use or on sale with the applicant's consent or allowance prior to the application; if deemed sufficiently useful and important, issue a patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specification / enablement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Before any inventor shall receive a patent he shall deliver a written description of his invention or discovery, and of the manner and process of making, constructing, using, and compounding the same, in such full, clear, and exact terms, avoiding unnecessary prolixity, as to enable any person skilled in the art or science ... to make, construct, compound and use the same; and shall particularly specify and point out the part, improvement, or combination, which he claims as his own invention or discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In case of a machine, fully explain the principle and several modes of application and how it differs from other inventions; specifications and claims guide scope of grant; defective or insufficient descriptions are a ground for objection by the Commissioner and may require amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings, specimens, and models requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Accompany the specification with a drawing or drawings, and written references, where the nature of the case admits of drawings; or with specimens of ingredients, and of the composition of matter, sufficient in quantity for the purpose of experiment; and furnish a model of his invention in all cases which admit of a representation by model, of a convenient size to exhibit advantageously its several parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Descriptions and drawings must be signed by the inventor and attested by two witnesses and filed in the Patent Office; drawings copies incur reasonable expense; models required when invention can be represented by model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath of originality and nationality
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant shall make oath or affirmation that he does verily believe that he is the original and first inventor or discoverer of the art, machine, composition, or improvement, for which he solicits a patent; and that he does not know or believe that the same was ever before known or used; and also of what country he is a citizen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The oath or affirmation may be made before any person authorized by law to administer oaths; when legal representatives apply after inventor's death, the oath is to be varied to suit them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commissioner examination and notification of defects/prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: On filing of the application, description and specification, and payment of duty, the Commissioner shall make, or cause to be made, an examination of the alleged new invention or discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Commissioner finds prior invention, prior patent, printed description, public use, sale, or defective/insufficient description, he shall notify the applicant, giving information and references useful for judging renewal/alteration of the application; applicant may withdraw (with partial refund) or persist and be required to swear anew; can appeal to board of examiners if not satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of examiners appeal process
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant persists after Commissioner's objection, he may, on appeal and request in writing, have the decision of a board of examiners of three disinterested persons appointed by the Secretary of State, one selected (if practicable) for skill in the particular art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board members take oath, are furnished with Commissioner's written certificate of objections, give reasonable notice to applicant and Commissioner, may reverse the decision of the Commissioner in whole or in part, and their opinion governs further proceedings. Applicant must pay $25 for a board; each examiner may receive not exceeding $10 for services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interfering applications / priority determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever an application would, in the opinion of the Commissioner, interfere with any other pending application or unexpired patent, the Commissioner must notify such applicants or patentees; dissatisfied parties may appeal to determine priority of right or invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proceedings for interfering applications follow like terms as board appeals; nothing in the act deprives an original inventor of rights because of prior foreign letters-patent published within six months before filing; applicant may request patent to date from time of filing (not exceeding six months prior).

rubrics_metrics.name: Secret filing of specifications and drawing (confidential archives)
rubrics_metrics.description: On request and payment of duty, an applicant's specification and drawings shall be filed in the secret archives of the office until he furnishes the model and the patent is issued, not exceeding the term of one year; applicant entitled to notice of interfering applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves priority while model or public disclosure is delayed; the applicant can also request an earlier effective date for the patent (up to six months prior to issue) under conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent form, recording, and term
rubrics_metrics.description: All patents shall be issued in the name of the Secretary of the United States, under the seal of the Patent Office, and signed by the Secretary of State, and countersigned by the Commissioner; and shall be recorded, together with the descriptions, specifications, and drawings, in books to be kept for that purpose. Every such patent shall contain a short description or title of the invention ... and in its terms grant ... for a term not exceeding fourteen years, the full and exclusive right and liberty of making, using, and vending the said invention, referring to the specifications for particulars, and specifying what the patentee claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent is a formal recorded instrument; the title/short description must correctly indicate nature and design; specifications annexed define the particulars of the grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees and filing payments (application and incidental fees)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before any application is considered the applicant shall pay into the Treasury or Patent Office: thirty dollars if citizen of United States (or resident alien with one year residency and oath of intention), five hundred dollars if subject of the King of Great Britain, three hundred dollars for all other persons. Duplicate receipts are taken and one filed in treasurer's office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Moneys received form the patent fund for payment of officers' salaries and office expenses. Other fees: copies (10 cents per 100 words), reasonable expense for copies of drawings, assignment recordation $3, caveat $20, board fee $25, withdrawal refund $20 (part of duty), examiners' fee up to $10 each.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat filing and protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Any inventor who desires further time to mature an invention may, on paying $20, file in the Patent Office a caveat setting forth the design and purpose, its principal and distinguishing characteristics, and praying protection of his right till he matures his invention; such caveat is filed in confidential archives and preserved in secrecy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If another person applies within one year for an interfering patent, Commissioner deposits description/specs/drawings/model in confidential archives and gives mail notice to caveat filer, who has three months to file full documents to avail himself of the caveat; caveat fee counts as part of later required duty if patent is later taken.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignments and recording
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent is assignable in law either as to the whole interest or any undivided part by instrument in writing; such assignment and every grant and conveyance of exclusive right under any patent shall be recorded in the Patent Office within three months from execution thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignee or grantee must pay the Commissioner the sum of three dollars for recording.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model relinquishment and partial refund on withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: If after notification of objection the applicant elects to withdraw his application, relinquishing his claim to the model, he shall be entitled to receive back twenty dollars, part of the duty required by the act, on filing written notice of such election in the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified copy of that notice by the Commissioner serves as warrant for the Treasurer to refund the amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Damages/remedies for infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any person without the consent of the patentee first obtained in writing shall make, devise, use, or sell the thing whereof the exclusive right is secured by such patent, such person shall forfeit and pay to the patentee ... a sum equal to three times the actual damage sustained by such patentee ... which sum shall be recovered by action on the case in the circuit court having jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides treble damages measured by actual injury; recovery through action on the case in circuit court.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue remedy for inadvertent noncompliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever any patent ... shall be invalid or inoperative by reason that any of the terms or conditions prescribed in the third section have not, by inadvertence, accident, or mistake, and without any fraudulent or deceptive intention, been complied with on the part of the inventor, it shall be lawful for the Secretary of State, upon the surrender to him of such patent, to cause a new patent to be granted to the inventor for the same invention for the residue of the period then unexpired, upon his compliance with the terms and conditions prescribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: New patent is liable to the same objections and defenses as an original patent; public use or privilege derived after the original grant does not prejudice right of recovery for violation after the reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent renewal/prolongation petitions to Congress (procedure and content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application to Congress to prolong or renew the term of a patent shall be made before its expiration, and shall be notified at least once a month for three months before presentation in two newspapers printed in Washington and in one newspaper in the State or territory where the patentee resides; the petition shall set forth particularly the grounds and shall be verified by oath; evidence may be taken before any judge or justice; accompanied by statement of ascertained value and receipts and expenditures showing profit or loss.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure establishes publicity and evidentiary requirements for Congressional petitions to extend patent term.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent office establishment, officers, appointments and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be established an office to be denominated the Patent Office attached to the Department of State; chief officer called Commissioner of Patents appointed by the President with Senate advice and consent; Commissioner to superintend, execute, and perform all acts respecting granting and issuing of patents and have custody of all books, records, papers, models, machines, and other things belonging to the office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commissioner entitled to specified compensation and postal privileges; may appoint chief clerk, examining clerk, clerks, machinist, messenger at specified salaries; commissioner and clerks disqualified from acquiring patent interests during appointment except by inheritance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oaths, bonds, seal, and certified copies as evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal officer and every person appointed shall, before entering duties, make oath or affirmation to faithfully execute trust; Commissioner and chief clerk shall give bonds with sureties to the Treasurer (Commissioner $10,000, chief clerk $5,000) to render true and faithful quarterly accounts of all moneys received; Commissioner shall cause a seal to be made; copies of records under signature of Commissioner (or chief clerk when vacant) with seal affixed shall be competent evidence in all cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bonds secure financial accountability; certified copies obtainable by paying prescribed fees; seal and signature create admissible evidence of office records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on officers acquiring patent interests
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commissioner, clerks, and every other person appointed and employed in the office shall be disqualified and interdicted from acquiring or taking, except by inheritance, during the period for which they hold their appointments, any right or interest, directly or indirectly, in any patent for an invention or discovery which has been, or may be hereafter, granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevents conflicts of interest between Patent Office personnel and patents under examination/grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights of deceased inventors and legal representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any person hath made ... any new invention on account of which a patent might be granted, and shall die before any patent shall be granted therefor, the right of applying for and obtaining such patent shall devolve on the legal representatives of such person in trust for the heirs at law or devisees, under the same conditions, limitations and restrictions as in his lifetime; when application is made by legal representatives, the oath shall be varied to apply to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preserves executor/administrator/devisee rights to pursue patent on behalf of decedent's estate subject to same formalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of expired patents list (annual duty of Secretary)
rubrics_metrics.description: It shall be the duty of the Secretary of State, annually in January, to report to Congress and to publish in two newspapers printed in Washington a list of all patents for discoveries, inventions, and improvements which shall have expired within the year immediately preceding, with the names of the patentees alphabetically arranged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency/public record of expired patents to inform public and Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent issue dating and limitation (dating from filing / six months rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the applicant shall request it, the patent shall take date from the time of filing of the specifications and drawings, not, however, exceeding six months prior to the actual issuing of the patent; and on like request and payment the specification and drawings may be filed in secret archives until model furnished and patent issued not exceeding one year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mechanism to fix effective priority date and to protect applicants during pre-issue period; limited to six months retroactive dating and one year secret holding for filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aliens' eligibility and conditions (residency/intention/public use)
rubrics_metrics.description: Privileges respecting patents given to citizens are extended to aliens who at time of petitioning shall have resided for two years within the United States (in earlier act) or shall be resident and have declared intention to become a citizen; person petitioning shall make oath that such invention hath not, to the best of his knowledge or belief, been known or used either in this or any foreign country; patents granted to aliens under some provisions shall cease and become void without resort to legal process if patentee fails within one year to introduce invention into public use in U.S., or if after introduction it does not continue publicly used and applied for six months, or if failure to become a citizen as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conditions and forfeiture rules for alien patentees; oath of novelty applies equally.

rubrics_metrics.name: No preclusion by board of examiners' opinion from judicial contest
rubrics_metrics.description: No opinion or decision of any board of examiners under the provisions of this act shall preclude any person interested in favor of or against the validity of any patent ... from the right to contest the same in any judicial court in any action in which its validity may come in question.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative determinations do not bar subsequent judicial review of patent validity.
